A prior agent black-box probed the jsonschema behavior family "array" of the program at /workspace/dataset/test13_executable (usage: /workspace/dataset/test13_executable --a '<instance json>' --b '<schema json>'; prints validator class, True/False, top-level error count).

Its findings were:
---
All results below are OBSERVED from 528 black-box runs of /workspace/dataset/test13_executable. Line 3 = number of TOP-LEVEL errors from iter_errors.

DISPATCH: `items` has three distinct implementations. (A) draft3/draft4 -> `_legacy_keywords.items_draft3_draft4`; (B) draft6/draft7/2019-09 -> legacy items_draft6_draft7_draft201909; (C) 2020-12 -> `_keywords.items` (pure "applies to every element at index >= len(prefixItems)").

items AS A SINGLE SCHEMA: identical in every draft. `{"items":{"type":"string"}}` on [1,2,3] -> False/3. Each element yields its OWN top-level error, and each FAILING KEYWORD inside the subschema also yields its own top-level error: `{"items":{"type":"string","minimum":10}}` on [1,2,3] -> 6 errors; `{"items":{"type":"integer","minLength":5}}` on ["a","b"] -> 4. Descended errors nest multiplicatively: `{"items":{"items":{"type":"string"}}}` on [[1,2],[3,4]] -> 4; `{"items":{"properties":{"a":{...},"b":{...}}}}` on two bad objects -> 4; `{"items":{"items":{"type":"integer"},"minItems":3}}` on [[1,2],[3,"x"]] -> 3. `items` never fires on non-array instances (0 errors, all drafts).

items AS AN ARRAY (tuple form): works in draft3, draft4, draft6, draft7 AND 2019-09 (all yield identical counts). [1,2,3] with items:[str,str,str] -> 3; items:[str] -> 1 (only index 0 checked); items:[] -> True/0; a tuple LONGER than the instance only checks min(len) positions (items:[{},{},{},{}] on [1,2,3] -> 0 errors; four failing schemas on a 3-array -> 3 errors). In 2020-12 array-form items is NOT tuple validation and NOT ignored — it CRASHES: `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'` raised from jsonschema/_keywords.py line 78 (items) -> validators.descend -> referencing/jsonschema.py `_dollar_id`, exit code 1, empty stdout, traceback on stderr. The crash happens only if at least one element is actually descended into: 2020-12 items:[...] on [] or on a non-array instance -> True/0 (no crash), and prefixItems:[{},{},{}] + items:[{"type":"string"}] on [1,2,3] -> True/0 (no leftover elements), but the same schema on [1,2,3,4] -> crash. Any non-boolean, non-object items value (string, number) crashes the same way in every draft that treats it as a schema (2020-12, 2019-09, draft6, draft7, draft4/3 crash too but with the bool/iterate path or descend path).

items AS A BOOLEAN: draft3 and draft4 CRASH unconditionally on items:true and items:false (`TypeError: 'bool' object is not iterable` at _legacy_keywords.py line 100 items_draft3_draft4), exit 1 — and it crashes even for the EMPTY array [] (only a non-array instance escapes, giving True/0). draft6/draft7/2019-09 treat boolean items as a schema applied to every element: items:false on [1,2,3] -> 3 errors (one per element), on [] -> 0; items:true -> 0. 2020-12 special-cases false: items:false on [1,2,3] -> exactly 1 error (an aggregate "too many items" error), prefixItems:[{"type":"integer"}] + items:false on [1,2,3] -> 1, prefixItems:[{},{},{}] + items:false on a 10-element array -> 1, on [] -> 0.

prefixItems: recognized ONLY by 2020-12. Completely ignored (0 errors) in draft3/4/6/7 AND 2019-09. 2020-12: prefixItems:[str,str,str] on [1,2,3] -> 3 errors; prefixItems:[str] -> 1; prefixItems:[] -> no-op; prefixItems:[true,false,true] on [1,2,3] -> 1 (the `false` at index 1). prefixItems must be a LIST: prefixItems:{} (empty object) -> True/0 by accident (zip over zero keys), prefixItems:{"a":{...}} (non-empty object) -> CRASH, prefixItems:true -> CRASH, prefixItems:"xyz" -> CRASH (exit 1). In 2020-12, `items` starts at index len(prefixItems).

additionalItems: honored in draft3, draft4, draft6, draft7, 2019-09; IGNORED entirely in 2020-12 (prefixItems + additionalItems:false -> True/0). Guard semantics: additionalItems does nothing unless `items` is present AND is a list. items absent -> ignored; items a dict/object -> ignored (items:{"type":"integer"} + additionalItems:false on [1,2,3] -> True/0); items a BOOLEAN -> CRASH `TypeError: object of type 'bool' has no len()` at _legacy_keywords.py line 113 additionalItems, in draft3/4 (crashes earlier in items), draft6, draft7 and 2019-09; a non-array instance escapes the crash (True/0). Counting: additionalItems:false yields exactly ONE aggregate error no matter how many extras (items:[{}] + additionalItems:false on a 5-array -> 1; items:[{},{},{}] + additionalItems:false on a 10-array -> 1). additionalItems as a SCHEMA yields one error PER extra element per failing keyword (items:[{}] + additionalItems:{"type":"string"} on [1,2,3] -> 2; on [1..5] -> 4). Tuple errors and additionalItems errors ADD: items:[int] + additionalItems:{int} on ["a","b","c"] -> 3 (1 tuple + 2 additional); items:[int,int] + additionalItems:false on ["a","b","c","d"] -> 3 (2 tuple + 1 aggregate); items:[false] + additionalItems:false on [1,2,3] -> 2.

contains: ignored in draft3 and draft4 (always 0 errors). Present in draft6+, and always yields AT MOST 1 top-level error (sub-errors go into context). `{"contains":{"type":"string"}}` on [1,2,3] -> 1; on [1,"a",3] -> 0; on [] -> 1 in draft6/7/2019-09/2020-12 (empty array always fails contains unless minContains:0); `contains:true` on [] -> 1; `contains:false` on [1] -> 1. Non-array instance -> 0. contains:"xyz" (non-schema) -> CRASH.

minContains/maxContains: recognized only in 2019-09 and 2020-12; silently ignored in draft6/draft7 (which still apply plain contains with an implicit min of 1). Key cross-draft divergence: `{"contains":{"type":"string"},"minContains":0}` on [1,2,3] or on [] gives False/1 in draft6 and draft7 (minContains ignored, contains still requires a match) but True/0 in 2019-09 and 2020-12. minContains/maxContains without `contains` are inert in every draft (0 errors). The contains family emits at most ONE error total: minContains:5 + maxContains:1 with 0 matches -> 1; minContains:2 + maxContains:1 with 3 matches -> 1 (only the maxContains violation); minContains:0 + maxContains:0 with 1 match -> 1; minContains:0 + maxContains:0 on [] -> 0. Floats work (minContains:2.0 -> ok with 3 matches); negative minContains:-1 -> ok. minContains:"x" -> CRASH.

uniqueItems: identical in every draft (draft3 through 2020-12), always at most ONE error regardless of how many duplicate groups ([1,1,2,2,3,3] -> 1; 200-element array with one dup -> 1; 500 objects with one dup -> 1). Equality is Python-like but with an explicit bool/number distinction: 1 vs 1.0 EQUAL (dup), 100 vs 1e2 EQUAL, 0 vs -0 EQUAL, [1] vs [1.0] EQUAL, {"a":1,"b":2} vs {"b":2,"a":1} EQUAL (key order irrelevant), [null,null] dup, ["a","a"] dup, [[1],[1]] dup, [{},{}] dup, [[[1],"a"],[[1],"a"]] dup. But booleans are NEVER equal to numbers at ANY depth: [1,true] unique, [0,false] unique, [{"a":false},{"a":0}] unique, [[false],[0]] unique, [{"a":[true]},{"a":[1]}] unique, [[{"x":true}],[{"x":1}]] unique. Cross-type non-equalities: [] vs {} unique, {} vs [] unique, "" vs 0 unique, null vs false unique, null vs 0 unique, 1 vs "1" unique. uniqueItems is TRUTHY-tested, not strictly boolean: uniqueItems:"yes" and uniqueItems:1 enforce uniqueness; uniqueItems:0 and uniqueItems:false do not. Non-array instances (strings, objects) -> 0 errors even with repeated chars/keys.

minItems/maxItems: identical in all drafts, one error each, and they ADD: {"minItems":5,"maxItems":1} on [1,2,3] -> 2 errors. minItems:3 on [1] -> 1; maxItems:1 on [1,2,3] -> 1; maxItems:0 on [1] -> 1; minItems:0 -> 0; minItems:-1 -> 0; floats compare numerically (minItems:2.5 on [1,2,3] -> 0, maxItems:2.5 on [1,2,3] -> 1). Non-array instance -> 0. Non-numeric values CRASH: minItems:"3" -> TypeError, maxItems:null -> TypeError (exit 1).

unevaluatedItems: recognized ONLY in 2019-09 and 2020-12; completely ignored (0 errors) in draft3/4/6/7. It yields AT MOST ONE top-level error, ever, regardless of how many items are unevaluated or how many keywords in its subschema fail: unevaluatedItems:false on a 10-element array -> 1; unevaluatedItems:{"minLength":5} on ["a","b","c"] -> 1; unevaluatedItems:{"type":"integer","minLength":5} on ["a","b","c"] -> 1. Crucially it is NOT a plain "no unevaluated items allowed" check — the subschema is actually applied and the error only appears if some unevaluated item FAILS it: unevaluatedItems:{"type":"integer"} on [1,2,3] -> True/0, on [1,"a"] -> 1, on ["a","b"] -> 1. unevaluatedItems:true / {} -> 0. Non-array instance -> 0. unevaluatedItems:"xyz" -> CRASH.
  Evaluation tracking (which indexes count as evaluated) is computed from the SAME schema object only, and includes: `items` when it is a schema/bool (marks ALL indexes evaluated, even if items itself produced errors — items:{"type":"string"} + unevaluatedItems:false on [1,2,3] -> 3 errors, not 4; items:{"type":"string"} + unevaluatedItems:{"type":"integer"} -> 3, not 4); `items` in tuple form under 2019-09 (items:[{},{},{}] covers all 3 -> 0 errors; items:[{},{}] leaves index 2 -> 1 error); `prefixItems` under 2020-12 only (prefixItems:[{},{},{}] + unevaluatedItems:false -> True/0 in 2020-12 but False/1 in 2019-09 where prefixItems is unknown); `additionalItems` under 2019-09 when items is a tuple (items:[{},{}] + additionalItems:{} + unevaluatedItems:false -> 0; with additionalItems:false -> 1 total, which is the additionalItems aggregate error, not an unevaluatedItems error); `contains` marks ONLY the MATCHING indexes evaluated (contains:{"type":"integer"} on [1,2,3] + unevaluatedItems:false -> 0; on [1,"a",3] index 1 stays unevaluated -> with unevaluatedItems:false -> 1, with unevaluatedItems:{"type":"string"} -> 0, with unevaluatedItems:{"type":"integer"} -> 1); and it recurses into allOf, anyOf, oneOf, if/then/else and $ref (allOf:[{prefixItems:[{},{},{}]}] -> 0; allOf:[{prefixItems:[{},{}]}] -> 1; allOf:[{items:{"type":"integer"}}] -> 0; allOf:[{contains:{"type":"integer"}}] -> 0; anyOf/oneOf covering branch -> 0; if:{prefixItems:[{const:1}]} + then:{prefixItems:[{},{},{}]} with matching if -> 0, with non-matching if and no else -> 1; if:{type:"string"} + else:{prefixItems:[{},{},{}]} -> 0; $ref:{prefixItems:[{},{},{}]} -> 0; $ref:{items:{"type":"integer"}} -> 0). `not` does NOT contribute evaluated indexes (not:{...} + unevaluatedItems:false -> 1). unevaluatedItems placed INSIDE an allOf branch does NOT see the parent's sibling prefixItems: {"allOf":[{"unevaluatedItems":false}],"prefixItems":[{},{},{}]} -> False/1.
  unevaluatedItems errors ADD to sibling errors: prefixItems:[{"type":"string"}] + unevaluatedItems:false on [1,2,3] -> 2 (1 prefixItems + 1 unevaluated); anyOf:[failing branch] + unevaluatedItems:false -> 2; contains fails + minContains:1 + unevaluatedItems:false on [1,2,3] with contains:{"type":"string"} -> 2; unevaluatedItems:false + minItems:5 (2019-09) -> 2.

COMBINED COUNTS observed: items 3-fail + minItems + maxItems + uniqueItems(unique) -> 5; items 3-fail + uniqueItems(dup) -> 4; items:{"type":"string"} + contains:{"type":"string"} on [1,2,3] -> 4 (3 items + 1 contains); type:"array" + items:{"type":"string"} + minItems:5 on [1,2,3] -> 4; uniqueItems + contains + minItems:5 + maxItems:2 + items:{"type":"string"} on [1,2,3] -> 6.

CRASH BEHAVIOR: every crash prints NOTHING on stdout, prints a Python traceback plus a `[PYI-NNN:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test13' due to unhandled exception!` line on stderr, and exits with code 1. 40 of the 528 vectors crash.
---
Gotchas it listed: ["2020-12 with array-form `items` does NOT ignore it and does NOT do tuple validation — it CRASHES (AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get', exit 1, empty stdout). But only if at least one element actually gets descended into: items:[...] on [], on a non-array instance, or fully covered by prefixItems yields True/0 with no crash.","2019-09 STILL supports tuple-form `items` + `additionalItems` (identical counts to draft7). Only 2020-12 dropped them. Do not lump 2019-09 with 2020-12 for items/additionalItems.","draft3 and draft4 CRASH on boolean `items` (true OR false) — 'bool' object is not iterable — even when the instance is the EMPTY array []. Only a non-array instance avoids the crash.","`additionalItems` CRASHES (object of type 'bool' has no len()) in draft6, draft7 and 2019-09 whenever `items` is a boolean. It is silently inert when items is absent or is an object/dict.","2020-12 `items:false` yields exactly ONE aggregate error (a 'too many items' style error), whereas draft6/7/2019-09 `items:false` yields ONE ERROR PER ELEMENT. Same for additionalItems:false (1 aggregate) vs additionalItems:{schema} (1 per extra element).","`prefixItems` is ignored in 2019-09 (not just in draft7) — 2019-09 does not know it at all, so prefixItems + unevaluatedItems:false behaves completely differently between 2019-09 and 2020-12.","`unevaluatedItems` NEVER produces more than 1 top-level error, even when 10 items each fail 2 keywords of its subschema. Do not descend-and-yield per item.","`unevaluatedItems` DOES apply its subschema (unevaluatedItems:{\"type\":\"integer\"} on [1,2,3] is VALID). It is not a bare 'nothing unevaluated allowed' check.","`items` marks all indexes evaluated for unevaluatedItems purposes EVEN WHEN items itself fails — so items:{\"type\":\"string\"} + unevaluatedItems:false on [1,2,3] gives 3, not 4.","`contains` marks only the MATCHING indexes as evaluated; non-matching indexes remain unevaluated and are then checked by unevaluatedItems.","`not` does not contribute evaluated indexes; allOf/anyOf/oneOf/if/then/else/$ref do. unevaluatedItems inside an allOf branch cannot see the parent schema's sibling prefixItems/items.","minContains:0 is a real draft-version fork: with contains and 0 matches it is VALID in 2019-09/2020-12 but INVALID (1 error) in draft6/draft7 where minContains is unknown and plain contains still requires >=1 match.","The whole contains/minContains/maxContains group emits AT MOST 1 top-level error, never 2, even when you construct minContains:5 + maxContains:1.","minItems and maxItems DO both fire (2 errors) when both are violated — unlike the contains group.","uniqueItems equality treats booleans as distinct from numbers at every nesting depth ([1,true] unique, [{\"a\":false},{\"a\":0}] unique) while treating 1 and 1.0 (and 100 vs 1e2, 0 vs -0) as equal. Object key order is irrelevant.","uniqueItems is truthiness-tested, not boolean-tested: uniqueItems:1 and uniqueItems:\"yes\" enforce uniqueness; uniqueItems:0 does not.","`contains` is completely ignored in draft3 and draft4 (0 errors even for contains:false).","Non-numeric minItems/maxItems (\"3\", null) and non-schema contains/minContains/items/prefixItems/unevaluatedItems values raise Python TypeError/AttributeError and exit 1 with empty stdout — no validation error, a hard crash.","prefixItems:{} (empty object) accidentally passes as a no-op in 2020-12, while prefixItems:{\"a\":{...}}, prefixItems:true and prefixItems:\"xyz\" crash.","Tuple-form items longer than the instance array only validates min(len(items), len(instance)) positions and never errors for the missing positions."]
Its vectors are in /workspace/probes/array.jsonl (528 lines of JSONL, each {"a","b","out","exit"}).

You are the COMPLETENESS CRITIC. Its assignment was:
Array keywords across drafts.
Probe: 'items' as a single schema vs as an ARRAY of schemas (tuple form) — in 2020-12 array-form items is NOT tuple validation anymore; determine exactly what 2020-12 does with items:[...] (is it treated as a schema? ignored? crash?) vs 2019-09 and draft7. 'prefixItems' (2020-12 only — is it ignored in 2019-09/draft7?). 'additionalItems' (draft4-2019-09; ignored in 2020-12?) with tuple items, with schema items, with false. 
Error counts: how many errors when 3 array elements each fail 'items'? When both items and additionalItems fail? 
'contains' (draft6+; ignored draft3/4?), 'minContains'/'maxContains' (2019-09+ only; ignored earlier?), minContains:0 special case, contains against empty array. 'uniqueItems' with [1,true],[1,1.0],[0,false],[{},{}],[[1],[1]], nested, with objects with reordered keys, large arrays. minItems/maxItems both failing. 'unevaluatedItems' (2019-09+) with prefixItems/items/contains/allOf/anyOf/if-then — probe carefully, and confirm it's ignored in draft7.
Report exact error counts for every case.

Your job: find what is MISSING or WRONG. Specifically:
1. Read /workspace/probes/array.jsonl (use head/wc/grep, don't dump the whole thing) and check which parts of the assignment were actually probed.
2. Identify untested edges, especially anything affecting ERROR COUNTS or cross-draft differences, and anything a JavaScript reimplementer would get wrong (unicode string length with astral chars, Python regex vs JS regex, float precision, integer vs bool, object key ordering, deep equality of numbers 1 vs 1.0, -0).
3. RUN those missing probes yourself against the executable and APPEND them as JSONL lines to the SAME file /workspace/probes/array.jsonl (same format: {"a","b","out","exit"}). Use a node script with execFileSync to append so escaping is exact. Never hand-write expected output.
4. Verify a random sample of ~8 existing lines by re-running them and comparing to the recorded "out" — report any mismatch (a mismatch means the file is corrupt/hand-written).

Return: family name, MERGED and CORRECTED findings prose (restate the full spec for this family incorporating both the prior findings and everything new you learned — the implementer reads ONLY your version, so it must be self-contained and complete), the vector file path, the TOTAL line count after your appends (wc -l), and a gotchas list.

ALL statements below are OBSERVED from 1099 black-box runs of /workspace/dataset/test13_executable (528 prior + 571 appended by me). Output line 1 = validator class, line 2 = True/False, line 3 = number of TOP-LEVEL errors from iter_errors. I re-ran 22 randomly sampled pre-existing lines and every one matched the recorded "out"/"exit" — the prior file is trustworthy. One prior claim was WRONG: the crash count is now 65/1099 (it was 44/528, not 40).

=== DRAFT DISPATCH ($schema) ===
"http://json-schema.org/draft-03/schema#" -> Draft3Validator; draft-04 -> Draft4Validator; draft-06 -> Draft6Validator; draft-07 -> Draft7Validator; "https://json-schema.org/draft/2019-09/schema" -> Draft201909Validator; "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema" -> Draft202012Validator. The trailing "#" is OPTIONAL and irrelevant ("http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema" -> Draft7Validator; ".../2019-09/schema#" -> Draft201909Validator). NO $schema key at all -> Draft202012Validator. An UNRECOGNIZED $schema URI ("http://example.com/unknown", "http://json-schema.org/schema#") does NOT crash and does NOT warn-out: it falls back to Draft202012Validator and validates normally. A NON-STRING $schema ("$schema":12) CRASHES (exit 1, empty stdout). A whole-schema boolean works: schema `true` on [1,2,3] -> True/0; schema `false` on [1,2,3] or on [] -> False/1. Schema `{}` -> True/0.

=== items AS A SINGLE SCHEMA (object) — identical in every draft ===
Applies to every element (in 2020-12, to every element at index >= len(prefixItems)). Each element yields its OWN top-level error, and each FAILING KEYWORD inside the subschema yields its own top-level error: items:{"type":"string"} on [1,2,3] -> 3; items:{"type":"string","minimum":10} on [1,2,3] -> 6; items:{"type":"integer","minLength":5} on ["a","b"] -> 4. Descent multiplies: items:{items:{"type":"string"}} on [[1,2],[3,4]] -> 4; items:{items:{"type":"string","minimum":10}} on [[1,2],[3,4]] -> 8; items:{items:{items:{"type":"string"}}} on [[[1]],[[2]]] -> 2; items:{properties:{a,b}} on two bad objects -> 4; items:{items:{"type":"integer"},"minItems":3} on [[1,2],[3,"x"]] -> 3. Counts scale linearly: 100-element array with items:{"type":"string"} -> 100 errors; 50-element array with items:{"type":"string","minimum":1000} -> 100 errors. items:{} -> 0 in all drafts. `items` NEVER fires on a non-array instance (0 errors, all drafts). type:"array" on a non-array short-circuits nothing but items/minItems simply do not fire: {"type":"array","items":{...},"minItems":5} on {"a":1} -> exactly 1 error (the type error) in draft7 and 2020-12.

=== items AS AN ARRAY (tuple form) ===
Tuple validation works in draft3, draft4, draft6, draft7 AND 2019-09 — all five produce identical counts. Only 2020-12 dropped it. items:[str,str,str] on [1,2,3] -> 3; items:[str] on [1,2,3] -> 1 (only index 0 checked); items:[] -> True/0; a tuple LONGER than the instance only checks min(len(items),len(instance)) positions (items:[{},{},{},{}] on [1,2,3] -> 0; four failing schemas on a 3-array -> 3). Multiple failing keywords per tuple position each count: items:[{"type":"string","minimum":10},{"type":"string","minimum":10}] on [1,2] -> 4. Nested: items:[{items:{"type":"string"}},{items:{"type":"string"}}] on [[1],[2]] -> 2. Booleans inside the tuple work: items:[false,false] on [1,2] -> 2; items:[true,true] -> 0.
In 2020-12 array-form items is NOT tuple validation and NOT ignored — it CRASHES with AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get' (jsonschema/_keywords.py line 78 -> validators.descend -> referencing/jsonschema.py _dollar_id), exit 1, empty stdout. The crash fires only if at least one element is actually descended into: 2020-12 items:[...] on [], on a non-array instance ("s"), or with prefixItems covering every index (prefixItems:[{},{},{}] + items:[{}] on [1,2,3]) -> True/0 with no crash; but the same schema on [1,2,3,4] -> crash. items:[] on [1,2,3] in 2020-12 -> CRASH; items:[{}]+additionalItems:false on [1,2,3] -> CRASH; allOf:[{items:[{},{},{}]}] on [1,2,3] -> CRASH; items:[{},{},{}]+unevaluatedItems:false on [1,2,3] -> CRASH.

=== items AS A BOOLEAN ===
draft3/draft4 CRASH unconditionally on items:true and items:false (TypeError: 'bool' object is not iterable, _legacy_keywords.py:100), exit 1 — even for the EMPTY array []. Only a non-array instance escapes (True/0).
draft6/draft7/2019-09 treat boolean items as a schema applied to every element: items:false on [1,2,3] -> 3 (one per element), on [] -> 0; items:true -> 0.
2020-12 special-cases false as an aggregate length check: items:false on [1,2,3] -> exactly 1 error; prefixItems:[{"type":"integer"}] + items:false on [1,2,3] -> 1; prefixItems:[{},{},{}] + items:false on a 10-element array -> 1; prefixItems:[{},{},{}] (or 4 entries) + items:false on [1,2,3] -> True/0; items:false on [] -> 0; items:true -> 0. prefixItems:[{"type":"string"}] + items:false on [1,2,3] -> 2 (1 prefixItems + 1 items aggregate).
Non-boolean non-object items values (string, number) crash in any draft that reaches descent (e.g. items:"xyz"), but 2020-12 prefixItems:[{},{},{}] + items:"xyz" on [1,2,3] -> True/0 because nothing is descended.

=== prefixItems ===
Recognized ONLY by 2020-12. Completely ignored (0 errors) in draft3/4/6/7 AND 2019-09. 2020-12: prefixItems:[str,str,str] on [1,2,3] -> 3; prefixItems:[str] on [1,2,3] -> 1; prefixItems:[str,str,str,str] on [1,2] -> 2 (only min(len) positions); prefixItems:[] -> no-op; prefixItems:[true,false,true] on [1,2,3] -> 1. Multiple failing keywords in one entry each count: prefixItems:[{"type":"string","minimum":10}] on [1] -> 2. Nested prefixItems multiply: prefixItems:[{prefixItems:[str,str]},{prefixItems:[str,str]}] on [[1,2],[3,4]] -> 4. prefixItems must be a LIST: prefixItems:{} (empty object) -> True/0 by accident, prefixItems:{"a":{...}} / true / "xyz" -> CRASH. In 2020-12 `items` starts at index len(prefixItems). additionalItems alongside prefixItems is ignored in 2020-12 (prefixItems:[{"type":"string"}]+additionalItems:false on [1,2,3] -> 1, only the prefixItems error).

=== additionalItems ===
Honored in draft3, draft4, draft6, draft7, 2019-09; IGNORED entirely in 2020-12. GUARD: additionalItems does nothing unless `items` is present AND is a LIST. items absent -> inert (additionalItems:false or {"type":"string"} or "nonsense" on [1,2,3] -> True/0). items a dict/object -> inert (items:{"type":"integer"}+additionalItems:false on [1,2,3] -> True/0). items a BOOLEAN -> CRASH TypeError: object of type 'bool' has no len() (_legacy_keywords.py:113) in draft6/draft7/2019-09 (draft3/4 crash earlier inside items); a non-array instance escapes.
VALUE SEMANTICS (this is a Python-truthiness dispatch, NOT a boolean/schema dispatch): if the value IS a JSON object -> it is used as a schema and descended into for every extra element; ELSE IF the value is FALSY (false, null, 0, 0.0, "", []) -> exactly ONE aggregate "additional items not allowed" error when extras exist; ELSE (truthy non-object: true, 1, "x", [1]) -> completely INERT, zero errors. Verified with items:[{}] on [1,2,3] in draft7 (and null re-checked in draft4 and 2019-09): null/0/[]/""/0.0/false -> 1 error each; true/1/"x"/[1] -> 0; {} -> 0 (descend into empty schema).
COUNTING: falsy additionalItems yields exactly ONE aggregate error no matter how many extras (items:[{}]+additionalItems:false on a 5-array -> 1; items:[{},{},{}]+additionalItems:false on a 10-array -> 1). Schema additionalItems yields one error PER extra element PER failing keyword (items:[{}]+additionalItems:{"type":"string"} on [1,2,3] -> 2; on [1..5] -> 4; items:[{"type":"string"}]+additionalItems:{"type":"string","minimum":10} on [1,2,3] -> 5 = 1 tuple + 2 extras x 2 keywords). Tuple errors and additionalItems errors ADD: items:[int]+additionalItems:{int} on ["a","b","c"] -> 3; items:[int,int]+additionalItems:false on ["a","b","c","d"] -> 3; items:[false]+additionalItems:false on [1,2,3] -> 2; items:[str,str,str]+additionalItems:false on [1,2,3] -> 3; items:[str,str]+additionalItems:{str} on [1,2,3,4] -> 4.
EMPTY TUPLE: items:[] is still a list, so the guard passes and additionalItems applies from index 0: items:[]+additionalItems:false on [1,2,3] -> 1; items:[]+additionalItems:{"type":"string"} on [1,2,3] -> 3; items:[]+additionalItems:true -> 0; items:[]+additionalItems:false on [] -> 0. (In 2020-12 items:[] on a non-empty array crashes first.)

=== contains / minContains / maxContains ===
`contains` is ignored in draft3 and draft4 (always 0 errors, even contains:false). Present in draft6, draft7, 2019-09, 2020-12, and the WHOLE group emits AT MOST 1 top-level error ever (sub-errors go into .context). contains:{"type":"string"} on [1,2,3] -> 1; on [1,"a",3] -> 0; on [] -> 1; contains:{} on [] -> 1; contains:true on [] -> 1; contains:false on [1] -> 1; contains:{"type":"string","minLength":5} on [1,"a",3] -> 1 (still 1, not 2). Non-array instance ("notarray", {"a":1}) -> 0. contains:"xyz" / 123 / [] -> CRASH.
minContains/maxContains are recognized ONLY in 2019-09 and 2020-12; SILENTLY IGNORED in draft6/draft7 (which still apply plain contains with an implicit minimum of 1). Cross-draft forks: contains:{"type":"string"},minContains:0 on [1,2,3] or on [] -> False/1 in draft6/draft7, True/0 in 2019-09/2020-12. contains:{"type":"integer"},maxContains:2 on [1,2,3] -> True/0 in draft6/draft7 (maxContains unknown, contains matches), False/1 in 2019-09/2020-12. maxContains:0 with matches -> 0 in draft6/7, 1 in 2019-09/2020-12. minContains:2 + contains:{"type":"string"} with 0 matches -> 1 in draft6/draft7 too (plain contains failure).
Without `contains`, minContains/maxContains are inert in EVERY draft (minContains:0 alone, maxContains:0 alone -> 0 errors). Never more than 1 error from the group: minContains:5+maxContains:1 with 0 matches -> 1; minContains:2+maxContains:1 with 3 matches -> 1; minContains:0+maxContains:0 with 1 or 3 matches -> 1; minContains:0+maxContains:0 with 0 matches -> 0; minContains:3+maxContains:3 with 3 matches -> 0; minContains:4 with 3 matches -> 1; contains+minContains:0+maxContains:5 on [] -> 0.

Negative values are accepted (minContains:-1 -> ok; minContains:-1+maxContains:-1 with 3 matches -> 1). minContains:"x" / null and maxContains:"2" -> CRASH.

=== uniqueItems ===
Identical in EVERY draft (draft3..2020-12) and always AT MOST ONE error regardless of how many duplicate groups ([1,1,2,2,3,3] -> 1; 200-element array with one dup -> 1; 500 objects with one dup -> 1). Non-array instances (strings with repeated chars, objects with repeated values) -> 0 errors.
VALUE IS PYTHON-TRUTHINESS-TESTED, not boolean-tested. On [1,1]: true, "yes", "false", "0", 1, 0.1, [0], [[]], {"a":1} all ENFORCE uniqueness (-> 1 error); false, 0, 0.0, -0, null, "", [], {} all SKIP the check (-> 0 errors). NOTE the JS trap: empty object {} and empty array [] are FALSY here (skip), while non-empty {"a":1} / [0] and the string "0"/"false" are TRUTHY (enforce).
EQUALITY (recursive, applied at every depth):
- numbers compare by VALUE after Python parsing: 1 == 1.0 == 1e0 (dup), 100 == 1e2 == 1E2 == 100.0, 0 == -0 == -0.0, 1e16 == 10000000000000000, 1e-7 == 0.0000001, 0.1 == 0.10000000000000001 (same IEEE double). Distinct doubles stay distinct: 1.0000000000000002 vs 1.0000000000000004 unique; 3 vs 3.0000000000000004 unique.
- ARBITRARY-PRECISION INTEGERS: Python ints are exact, so 9007199254740993 vs 9007199254740992 are UNIQUE, and 123456789012345678901234567890 vs ...891 are UNIQUE. (A JS implementation using Number would wrongly call these duplicates.) Identical big ints are still dups.
- Overflow: 1e400 parses to inf, so [1e400,1e400] AND [1e400,1e401] are both DUPS (inf == inf).
- BOOLEANS ARE NEVER EQUAL TO NUMBERS at any depth: [1,true], [0,false], [true,1.0], [false,0.0], [false,-0.0], [{"a":false},{"a":0}], [[false],[0]], [[[false]],[[0.0]]], [{"a":[true]},{"a":[1]}], [{"a":[true]},{"a":[1.0]}], [[{"x":true}],[{"x":1}]] are all UNIQUE. [true,true] and [false,false] are dups; [true,false] is unique.
- objects: key ORDER irrelevant ({"a":1,"b":2} == {"b":2,"a":1}); values compared with the same numeric rules ({"a":1} == {"a":1.0}, {"a":1,"b":2} == {"a":1.0,"b":2.0}, {"a":-0} == {"a":0.0}); nested arrays/objects recurse ([1,[2.0]] == [1.0,[2]], {"a":[1,{"b":2}]} dup, {"a":{}} dup).
- cross-type non-equalities: [] vs {}, "" vs 0, null vs false, null vs 0, 1 vs "1", [1] vs ["1"] are all UNIQUE. [null,null], [[null],[null]], [{"a":null},{"a":null}], [[],[]], [{},{}], [[[]],[[]]], ["a","a"], [[1],[1]], [[[1],"a"],[[1],"a"]] are DUPS.
- strings compare by exact code-point sequence with NO Unicode normalization: "é" (NFC) vs "é" (NFD) are UNIQUE; two identical astral strings "😀" are dups.

=== STRING SUB-KEYWORDS REACHED THROUGH items (Python semantics a JS port will get wrong) ===
maxLength/minLength count Unicode CODE POINTS, not UTF-16 units: ["😀"] (one astral emoji) passes items:{"maxLength":1} and FAILS items:{"minLength":2}; ["😀😀"] passes maxLength:2. Decomposed sequences count their parts: ["é"] passes maxLength:1 but ["é"] FAILS maxLength:1.
`pattern` is Python `re.search` (substring match, not anchored): pattern:"b" matches "abc". Python-only regex behaviour observed: "$" matches BEFORE a trailing newline, so pattern:"^a$" MATCHES "a\n" (True/0) — JS would reject it; "^" is NOT multiline, so pattern:"^b" does NOT match "a\nb"; "\Z" is supported (pattern:"a\\Z" matches "a", "^ab\\Z" matches "ab") — JS treats \Z as literal "Z"; inline flags work (pattern:"(?i)ABC" matches "abc", "(?i)abc" matches "ABC", "(?s)a.b" behaves as a normal dot and does NOT match "ab"); "." matches a whole astral code point (pattern:"^.$" matches "😀") whereas JS without /u would need two units; "\d" is UNICODE-aware and matches Arabic-Indic "٠" (JS \d is ASCII-only); "\w" matches "é"; POSIX classes are NOT supported ("[[:alpha:]]" does not match "x").
`type` distinguishes bool from number in every draft: items:{"type":"integer"} on [true] -> 1 error, on [true,false] -> 2; items:{"type":"number"} on [true] -> 1; items:{"type":"boolean"} on [1] -> 1; items:{"type":"integer"} on [1] -> 0 and on [1.5] -> 1.

Every crash prints NOTHING on stdout, prints a Python traceback plus "[PYI-NNN:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test13' due to unhandled exception!" on stderr, and exits 1. 65 of the 1099 vectors crash.
